{
 "iri": "https://beatscript.app/ontology/concept/tool-beatscript-check",
 "label": "check",
 "types": [
  "https://beatscript.app/ontology/ns#McpTool"
 ],
 "definition": "Check a BeatScript program without playing it: parse, type-check and compile the text. ALWAYS call check before eval, share or render, and fix every error at its line:col before trying again: a program with an error is refused whole. Warnings do not block. A `control:` line is the control deck (docs/BEATSCRIPT.md "The control deck"): engine calls only (move, swap pairs, load pair, queue, crossfader, a timed tempo, duck, mix, do), beside deck A:, deck B: and master:, sequenced by sections like a deck; it checks and plays as the same line with no head. An `arrange { }` switches it pass by pass with a line of its own: `~ control off` (a section's control-deck lines do not fire from here on), `~ control on`, `@ control off` (the next section only), `~ control freeze off` (the lines of one call), `~3 control off` (every 3rd pass); plays[].control_off in the answer's arrange names the calls each play holds back.

Answers {ok, errors, warnings, diagnostics[{severity, line, col, end_col, message, expected, found, help, render}], cid, canonical, version, renamed_cid, expanded_cid, tempo, key, sections, song_bars, seconds, evolve, uses_assets, restricted, docs}, and refs and resolution for a program with references, and arrange {passes, unbounded, plays[{section, name, pass, coda, start_bar, bars, reads, control_off}], patterns, fires} for an `arrange { }` with mutations. docs is the text's doc comments, [{kind, name, doc}]: the `#` lines directly above a section, let, def or arrange (a comment, so the CID does not change); sections[].doc is a section's, when it has one. line and col are 1-based; help says what would fix it ("did you mean ..."); render is the same error in caret form. ok:false is an answer, not a tool error. cid and canonical are of the canonical text (comments and spacing do not change the CID). version is the language version: 2 for a text whose header has `#! beatscript 2` (write that), 1 for a text with `#! btw 1` or no version line (BeatScript 1, the old spelling, which checks as before and keeps its old CID); renamed_cid is the CID of the same program in the other version (fmt upgrades a BeatScript 1 text to it). A station program (radio: a `station { }` block, see the station tool) checks the tracks of its first pass of forms and its first segue, and the answer gains station {text, cid, genre, generator, seed, step, forms, tempo, key, length, start_cid, version, tracks, segue}.

With same_as (another program's CID or text) the answer gains same_as {same, text_same, basis, why, diffs[{section, deck, start_bar, a_cid, b_cid}], only_in_a, only_in_b, renamed, song, diff}: whether the two are the same song by their compiled nets and song-level settings, not their text. When they are not, diff says what changed in music: diff.summary is one line per change ("tempo 124 -> 126", "moved outro: bar 13 -> bar 5", "drop2 bass = drop bass transposed +1", "drop bass: 1 note changed (1:7 c3 -> d3)"), with song, arrangement (inserted, removed, moved, repeated, renamed, changed) and parts (a transform: transpose, octave, rotate, reverse, thin, fill, fast, slow; else the notes added, removed or changed at bar:step) as JSON. Use it to prove a refactor changed nothing, or to find what an edit did.

This is the loop for writing a program (there is no compose tool): read https://beatscript.app/docs/cheatsheet.md and one or two list_examples programs, call instruments, write the program (its first line `#! beatscript 2`), call check and fix every line:col error until ok, then eval / load to play it and share to store it. Voices come from the instruments tool: use only names from it. For a sung line, a public-domain phrasebook line (list_examples with phrasebook true) comes with its meter, stress and phoneme escapes, so that sing @id on melody checks with no unknown-word warning (https://beatscript.app/docs/found-phrases.md). A voice name with a leading digit (808-bass) cannot be written: inst=808-bass reads as 808 - bass and a quoted "808-bass" is refused, so pick a voice that starts with a letter (inst=sub-bass for a deep bass). Read-only, no sign-in. Limits: the text is at most 16384 bytes; about 60 calls a minute.

References: a program can call the seeded generator (gen@2 techno seed=42 section=drop part=bass is the program generate prints, fitted to the program's key and tempo unless it says bpm= or key=) or borrow from seed(...), template(...) or a stored program by CID. Its cid is of the text as written (the recipe), and the answer says what the recipe makes: refs lists each reference of the program (a gen@N call, a seed(...), a template(...), a <cid>.section borrowed from a stored program): its kind, half (engine or structure), call, place (part, let, section or arrange), name, line and col, resolved (the CID it is pinned to), generator, fitted (what a gen call took from the program: key, bpm) and track; expanded_cid is the CID of the program with every reference written out as plain BeatScript: cid addresses the recipe, expanded_cid the result; the same recipe always gives the same expanded_cid, and a program with no references has expanded_cid equal to cid; resolution is the manifest: each reference once, with the CID it is pinned to and the generator and version that made it (seeded@2), and for a gen call the key and bpm it was generated in; a template's entry in resolution has parts: each role its reference binds, at any depth (a role of a form bound to a role is a part of that part), as {path, role, kind, call, cid, resolves, generator, parts}: path is where it stands (episodes/ground), kind what it was bound to (gen, stored, theme, notes or template), call the source as bound, cid the CID of what it is written out as (a program of its own: the key and tempo it plays in and the lines its binding wrote, every reference in them written out), resolves the CID its source is pinned to; the same recipe always gives the same parts and part CIDs. With expand true, each entry of refs also carries its expansion (the BeatScript it is written out as where it stands), and each part its text. A diagnostic of severity info at each gen call says the CID it resolved to and the key and tempo it was fitted to; the expand tool writes the whole program out. A `use SOURCE as NAME` line names a source on a line of its own (a stored program's <cid>.drop or <cid>.drop.bass, a gen call, a canned section template(passacaglia).ground, a form, theme ode_to_joy, phrase @tempest_such_stuff, genre@1 techno.drop; docs/BEATSCRIPT.md "Name a source: `use`"), and the name is then used as a section, a let or a phrase of the program's own (in a role, as its source): it is a reference of kind `use` in refs, a note at it says what the name is, and imports lists each `use SOURCE as NAME` line of the program: its name, what the name is (is: a section, a line, a source for a role or a phrase), from (the source, in canonical spelling), source (its kind: stored, gen, template, form, theme, phrase or genre), resolved (what it is pinned to: a CID, or the library's CID for a theme or a phrase), line and col, and what (a sentence).

Lexicon harvest, a side effect with no flag: when the program checks and may be kept (no samples or loops, no `use restricted`, public visibility; push_private records nothing), the (word, phonemes) pairs of its lyrics are recorded to grow the CC0 lexicon: each annotated escape word=/phonemes/ (jingle=/j ii ng g uh l/ sings the escape and keeps the word) and each word no lexicon knows, with the rules' pronunciation. Only the word, its phonemes and the program's CID are kept, never the text. The answer's lexicon is {harvested, new}: the pairs taken from this program, and how many no program had given before. When check says a word is not in the lexicon and it sounds wrong, write it as word=/phonemes/."
}
